title: Special Topics
description: Individual or group study of selected topics in applied physiology and sport management.

title: Specials Topics
description: Individual or group study of selected topics in applied physiology and sport management.

title: Introduction to Sport Management
description: Explores the functional areas of business, management principles, contemporary issues, and future considerations for organizations within the fitness and sports industries. Gateway course for sport management concentration majors; successful completion is mandatory to be invited into the program. Recommended corequisite: APSM 3322, APSM 3332, APSM 3340, or APSM 3372. Reserved for students with fewer than 90 credit hours.

title: Coaching and Leadership for Performance
description: Examines what coaches do, the qualities of expert coaches, strategies for effective and cohesive programs, a sound coaching philosophy, and the art and science of coaching. Serves as the gateway course to the major. Students must complete this course with a C- or better in order to qualify for the sport performance leadership major. Recommended corequisite: APSM 3300, APSM 3315, APSM 3322, APSM 3332, or APSM 3351. Reserved for students with fewer than 90 credit hours.

title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I With Laboratory
description: A systemic approach to the study of the human body, with a focus on the anatomical structure and function of the human neuromusculoskeletal systems. Gateway course for applied physiology and enterprise concentration majors; successful completion is mandatory for admission to the program. Lab fee: $30. APSM 2441 is cross-listed with BIOL 2441; you may not receive credit for both APSM 2441 and BIOL 2441.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Restricted to students who have fewer than 90 credit hours or have the instructor’s approval.

title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II With Laboratory
description: Examines the gross anatomy and physiology of the endocrine, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, and urinary systems, and their relationship with human health and performance. Lab fee: $30. APSM 2442 is cross-listed with BIOL 2442; you may not receive credit for both APSM 2442 and BIOL 2442.

title: Anatomy for Movement
description: Explores the anatomy of bones and muscles and their role in normal muscle function and common gross motor movements. Cannot be taken by APSM majors in APHM concentration or by APHM or AP minors.

title: Rules and Regulations of Sport
description: Explores the rules, interpretation, mechanics, and philosophies of officiating selected sports on a basic level. Sports likely to be covered include (but are not limited to) football, volleyball, basketball, and soccer.

title: Applied Exercise Physiology
description: Uses an organ system approach to examine the body’s responses and adaptations to exercise and movement. Recommended: APSM 3322.

title: Communication in Sport
description: Facilitates the improvement of communication skills for coaches through the introduction of various communication styles and techniques and furthers an understanding of conflict resolution and negotiation.

title: Biomechanics
description: Introduces the mechanical basis of function and dysfunction in human movement. Newtonian mechanics and musculoskeletal biology are integrated to provide the necessary foundation for clinical and performance-based professions. Course fee: $30. Recommended: PHYS 1303, MATH 1304. APSM majors and minors only.

title: Functional Biomechanics
description: Introduces the scientific basis of support and motion in humans and other vertebrate animals, drawing equally on musculoskeletal biology and Newtonian mechanics.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: APSM 2340; or prerequisite or corequisite: APSM 2310.

title: Legal and Ethical Aspects of Applied Physiology and Sports Management
description: Creates an important awareness of the legal and ethical implications of some of the situations that can arise in the careers of sports, coaching, and health and fitness professionals. These legal and ethical aspects include those related to safety, risk management, personnel, contracts, constitutional rights, employment issues, discrimination concerns, and collective bargaining and unions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite or corequisite: APSM 2310; or prerequisite: APSM 2340 or APSM 2441 or BIOL 2441.

title: Coaching Team Sports
description: Develops fundamental instructional techniques utilized for coaching various team sports. Emphasis is placed on the analysis of skills, discussion of developmental appropriateness, organization, key terms, and other teaching/coaching strategies. Sports likely to be covered include (but are not limited to) football, volleyball, basketball, and soccer.

title: Applied Management Skills in Sports and Fitness
description: An extensive study of organizational functions, methods of operation, and types of ownership. Also explores the role of organizations in contemporary society as they relate to fitness and sport enterprises today.
prerequisites: Prerequisite APSM 2441 or BIOL 2441; or prerequisite or corequisite APSM 2310.

title: Health Promotion Practice
description: Focuses on understanding, influencing, and modifying health status and behaviors in populations. Explores the assessment, planning, execution, and evaluation of health promotion programming, as well as different applications and delivery methods of health promotion.

title: Nutrition
description: Examines the role that nutrition plays in health and optimal function, including the impact and research of nutrition on obesity, heart disease, stroke, cancer, eating disorders, and specific populations. Explores food technology--including microorganisms in food-borne illness; advantages and disadvantages of canning; pasteurization; use of preservatives; the use of irradiation as a preservative; the process, risks, and benefits of genetic modification; food additives; and pesticides’ safety concerns.

title: Applied Physiology and Health Management Professional Seminar
description: Prepares students who aspire to careers in the health and fitness industries. Topics include the fundamentals of leadership and management. Requires visits to off-campus fitness and health-related facilities for which students must provide their own transportation.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Restricted to APHM majors only.

title: Nutrition and Population Health
description: Introduces current societal issues concerning public health nutrition and examines the nature of poverty, food security, and hunger at the community, regional, and national levels. Emphasis is placed on personal experience via community engagement, the applicability of cutting-edge research on creating effective national policies, and advocacy campaigns for low-income Americans. Finally, this course reviews existing local and national programs and policies, including strengths, weaknesses, and areas for modification or new interventions.

title: Cultural Intelligence in Sport and Health
description: Explores how historical and contemporary practices in society have shaped the opportunities and experiences of various cultural groupings in sport. In particular, the course focuses on diversity issues in sport coaching as they relate to race, ethnicity, gender, socioeconomic class, sexuality, religion, and ability/disability.

title: Advanced Public Relations in Sport
description: Examines the role of public relations specific to the industry of sport, focusing on the conceptual, strategic, and technical understanding of the operation and business of public relations in sport communication.

title: Technology and Sport
description: An overview of the role technology plays in modern coaching, specifically in student-athlete development, monitoring, and recruitment. Emphasizes organization of team and individual video analysis, tactics of competition, and administration of an athletic program. Also covers scouting opponents, determining playing time, and making annual training plans. Junior and senior standing only.

title: Exercise Physiology With Laboratory
description: Examines the physiological mechanisms underlying human movement. Topics include muscle physiology, respiration, cardiac function, circulation, energy metabolism, and their application to training. Students are expected to have a basic understanding of algebra, general chemistry, and anatomy and/or physiology prior to enrollment. Lab fee: $30.

title: Independent Study in Applied Physiology and Sport Management
description: For APSM majors or minors seeking to increase their experiential presence and/or research capabilities. Enrollment is by faculty invitation only. Minimum 60 credit hours.

title: Teaching Practicum
description: Students assist the instructor in conducting a course in which they have previously excelled. Maximum of 3 credit hours allowed. APSM majors or minors only.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, A- or better for any previous enrollment in this course, and instructor approval.

title: Experiential Learning Lab
description: Explores practical and theoretical aspects of the discipline with hands-on experience in the sport-coaching industry. Possible topics and/or activities include shadowing a coach, working on a community outreach project, and satisfying professional certification requirements. A total of 3 credit hours from among APSM 4190, APSM 4290, and APSM 4390 are required for the sport performance leadership concentration.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Instructor approval and junior standing (minimum of 60+ hours).

title: Independent Study in Applied Physiology and Sport Management
description: For APSM majors or minors seeking to increase their experiential presence and/or research capabilities. Enrollment is by faculty invitation only. Minimum 60 credit hours.

title: Teaching Practicum
description: Students assist the instructor in conducting a course in which they have previously excelled. Maximum of 3 credit hours allowed. APSM majors or minors only.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, A- or better for any previous enrollment in this course, and instructor approval.

title: Research Practicum in Applied Physiology
description: Intended for students considering a career in laboratory-based biological research. Students conduct supervised research with an APSM research faculty member in his/her laboratory. Enrollment is by invitation from an APSM research faculty member in whose lab the research is conducted.

Possible topics and/or activities include shadowing a coach, working on a community outreach project, and satisfying professional certification requirements. A total of 3 credit hours from among APSM 4190, APSM 4290, and APSM 4390 are required for the sport performance leadership concentration.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Instructor approval and junior standing (minimum of 60+ hours).

title: Applied Physiology, Research, and Ethics
description: An overview of the concepts and procedures necessary for understanding scientific research, designing research projects, and interpreting research findings. Course content focuses on the steps involved in conducting a research project, including identification of research questions, developing hypotheses when appropriate, conducting background literature review, selecting appropriate research design, analyzing data, and reporting research findings. This is a writing intensive course involving the preparation of a well-written research proposal in topics related to physiology, medicine, health, exercise, and sports science.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: STAT 2331. Restricted to APHM specialization majors, senior standing only.

title: Psychology of Sport
description: Explores various psychological theories and research related to sport and exercise behavior.

title: Principles of Exercise is Medicine
description: Discusses the physiological and medicinal role exercise plays in the promotion of health and the prevention and treatment of disease. Students evaluate health behaviors and risk factors of disease; techniques to administer health assessments; and assess, design, and implement exercise programs for healthy and special populations.

title: Physiology in Health and Disease
description: Addresses the hemodynamic principles, neural and local regulatory mechanisms, and molecular pathways associated with the physiologic adaptations to exercise training and pathological alterations associated with disease. Students gain laboratory experience and participate in discussions related to current research topics in the field of exercise. Course fee: $30.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: APSM 2441, APSM 2442, APSM 3411. Restricted to APSM majors and minors only.

title: Special Topics in Sport Management
description: A flexible platform for the exploration of current trends, emerging issues, and specialized topics in sport management. The specific focus of the course varies each semester based on faculty expertise and developments in the sport industry. Students gain timely insights into contemporary challenges and innovations shaping the field of sport management.

title: Senior Project
description: Teaches the process of formal inquiry by utilizing a team format to plan, execute, and report results regarding a scientific question of interest to the group. Senior standing only (at least 90 credit hours required).
prerequisites: Prerequisites: STAT 2331 is required for applied physiology and health management and sport management concentrations. Restricted to APSM majors.

title: Pandemics! The Science of Disease Spread, Prevention, and Control
description: Explores the science of epidemic and pandemic prevention, treatment, and control, and examines what we’ve learned from pandemics across time, ranging from the bubonic plague to COVID 19.

title: Sports Marketing
description: This course provides a strategic framework to understand market dynamics, trends, consumer behavior, products, delivery systems, and marketing and promotional strategies that shape and drive the sports marketing industry.

title: Health Care: From Policy to Practice
description: Explores the development and transformation of health care policy; the environmental factors that influence the delivery of health care services; and the financial, economic, and operational issues related to health care.

title: Motor Learning
description: Focuses on the principles of learning as they relate to the acquisition and development of motor skills, motor performance, and motor learning throughout life. Also covers learning in the context of sports and performance-related skills acquisition.

title: Creating Global and Public Health Impact
description: Interdisciplinary approach to creating sustainable impact in global, public, and population health. Taught by engaging discussions, case studies, and helping local health organizations solve difficult institutional and community challenges.

title: Independent Study in Applied Physiology and Sport Management
description: For APSM majors or minors seeking to increase their experiential presence and/or research capabilities. Enrollment is by faculty invitation only. Minimum 60 credit hours.

title: Teaching Practicum
description: Students assist the instructor in conducting a course in which they have previously excelled. Maximum of 3 credit hours allowed. APSM majors or minors only.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, A- or better for any previous enrollment in this course, and instructor approval.

title: Directed Studies in Applied Physiology
description: This directed research course is necessary to be considered for departmental distinction. Students must have an APSM faculty sponsor and a written structured course plan to enroll.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Instructor invitation, APSM 4361, senior standing, 3.000 overall GPA, and 3.500 GPA within the major.

title: Directed Studies in Sport Management
description: This directed research course is necessary to be considered for departmental distinction. Students must have an APSM faculty sponsor and a written structured course plan to enroll.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Instructor approval, APSM 4359, senior standing, 3.000 overall GPA, and 3.500 GPA within the major.

title: Directed Studies in Applied Physiology and Enterprise
description: This directed research course is necessary to be considered for departmental distinction. Students must have an APSM faculty sponsor and a written structured course plan to enroll.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Instructor approval; APSM 4159, APSM 4259, or APSM 4359; senior standing; 3.000 overall GPA; and 3.500 GPA within the major.

title: Strength and Conditioning Programs
description: Examines the essentials of strength training and conditioning that are key to completion of the Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist certification and the Certified Personal Trainer certification.

title: Coaching Seminar: Special Topics
description: A discussion-based course examining contemporary issues, emerging research, and key standards in sport coaching. Example topics may include (but are not limited to) long-term athlete development, coach as an administrator, ethics, and youth sport participation.

title: Revenue in Sports
description: This course covers sports industry revenue topics, including professional league and team revenue generation, franchise ownership and valuation, corporate sponsorship, sports media revenue, and industry selling practices.

title: Sport Facility and Event Management
description: This course examines the principles of sport facility planning, design, and management. Topics include venue design, operations, revenue streams, budgeting, personnel, security, media relations, crisis control, and legal considerations.

title: Professional Development in Sport Management
description: Provides a comprehensive overview of the various segments of the sport and allied-sport industries. Students assess their personal and career skills, competencies, and interests as well as learn how to investigate internship and job opportunities; choose careers in line with their skills, competencies, and interests; and market themselves to prospective employers. (Students are required to provide their own transportation to and from off-campus sports-related organizations and/or events if assigned.) Prerequisites: APSM 2310, one 3000-level APSM course, and 30 credit hours.
prerequisites: Restricted to applied physiology and sport management (sport management concentration) majors only.

title: Sports Data and Analytics
description: Examines the theory, development, and application of data and analytics in sports. Explores recent trends in sports data and analytics from a practical perspective, teaching students the skills and ideas to understand and utilize analytics to create value for sport enterprises.

title: Exercise Program Design
description: Focuses on evidence-based exercise prescriptions that promote health and maximize performance in the elite and recreational athlete.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: APSM 3311; or APSM 2441 and APSM 3411.

title: Experiential Learning Lab

Possible topics and/or activities include shadowing a coach, working on a community outreach project, and satisfying professional certification requirements. A total of 3 credit hours from among APSM 4190, APSM 4290, and APSM 4390 are required for the sport performance leadership concentration.

title: Applied Physiology and Enterprise Internship
description: Experiential learning at a local fitness or health organization as an intern for a total of 250 hours. (Students are required to provide their own transportation to and from their assigned off-campus fitness and/or health-related internship site.) Prerequisites: APSM 4351 and senior standing.

title: Research Practicum in Applied Physiology
description: Intended for students considering a career in laboratory-based biological research. Students conduct supervised research with an APSM research faculty member in his/her laboratory. Enrollment is by invitation from an APSM research faculty member in whose lab the research is conducted.

title: Sport Management Internship
description: Experiential learning at a local sports industry organization as an intern for a total of 250 hours. (Students are required to provide their own transportation to and from their assigned off-campus sports-related internship site.) Prerequisites: APSM 4373 and senior standing.

title: How People Learn with AI
description: Designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge to understand how adults learn, with a unique focus on how learning takes place through the augmentation of different technologies. Students develop a critical understanding of social, educational, and ethical concerns related to the advent of technologies across the last 25 years, from the widespread use of the Internet and instant messaging to the latest developments in Generative AI. Students analyze a variety of use cases of technology within the context of teaching and learning in secondary and higher education; demonstrate an understanding of the ethical considerations involved; describe the emergence of AI technologies as part of a trajectory of technology-enhanced pedagogy; apply different learning theories to the university context; and evaluate contemporary academic integrity issues. Students will be able to describe key educational theories; apply those theories to secondary and post-secondary education; critically evaluate key technology-enhanced learning tools; and analyze the ethical, social, and cultural contexts within educational settings pertaining specifically to AI use in the context of higher education.

title: Introduction to Diverse Learners
description: A study of diversity, multicultural concepts, and inclusion. Also, explores issues, policies, and professional practice relevant to teaching.

title: Educational Psychology
description: This course focuses on aspects related to the learning process, such as education theories, characteristics of learners, nature and measurements of abilities, motivation, and successful classroom practice.

title: Literacy and Society
description: A structured service learning opportunity that fosters academic growth, citizenship, leadership, and civic responsibility. Readings and course activities relate to the relationship between literacy and society. Throughout the term, students tutor local elementary school students and complete related assignments.

title: Community Partnerships
description: Integrates academic knowledge with community engagement, providing students a unique opportunity to apply theoretical concepts in real world settings. Through volunteer work in the Dallas community, students develop critical thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills while fostering cultural competence and civic responsibility. By addressing local issues and collaborating with diverse community partners, students enhance their understanding of social justice, ethics, and interdisciplinary approaches to community development. Prepares students to be informed, ethical, and engaged citizens, equipped to navigate complex societal challenges and contribute positively to their communities. Centers on active, immersive engagement with the local Dallas community through service-learning projects that strategically align with one’s academic focus.

title: Foundations of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
description: Students will develop/analyze lesson plans in all content areas using TESOL competencies, emphasizing language concepts, acquisition, teaching and assessment strategies, and the role of culture in language acquisition.

title: Special Topics
description: Students work on a personalized system of instruction. Most of the work in this course is done as an independent study.

title: Field Experience I
description: Provides students opportunities to work in appropriate school settings and allows them to observe a functioning classroom. Includes classroom setup, environment, organization, structure, and discipline.

title: Field Experience II
description: With a focus on special populations, this course places students in school settings where they observe the teaching techniques used to help children with exceptional needs.

title: Field Experience III
description: Provides students opportunities to work in appropriate school settings and to plan and teach lessons. Students shadow a teacher in preparation for student teaching.

title: Field Experience I: Secondary
description: This course gives students opportunities to work in appropriate school settings and allows them to observe a functioning classroom. Includes classroom setup, environment, organization, structure, and discipline.

title: Field Experience II: Secondary
description: Places students in elementary school settings where they observe the teaching techniques used to help children with exceptional or special needs.

title: Field Experience III: Secondary
description: This course gives students opportunities to work in appropriate school settings and to plan and teach lessons. Students shadow a teacher in preparation for student teaching.

title: Practicum for Teaching Early Reading and Writing
description: Provides experience applying evidence-based principles of literacy development and learning in young children, early childhood through second grade. Requires tutoring experiences in a local school.

title: Special Topics
description: Students work on a personalized system of instruction. Most of the work in this course is done as an independent study.

title: Methods for Teaching Early Reading and Writing
description: Examines evidence-based principles of literacy development and learning in young children, early childhood through second grade. Focuses on designing, adapting, and evaluating beginning literacy instruction for children.

title: Special Topics
description: Students work on a personalized system of instruction. Most of the work in this course is done as an independent study.

title: Formative/Summative Assessment
description: Explanation and practice of formal and informal assessment strategies, the ways assessment outcomes should inform instruction, and the methods for sharing assessment outcomes with families. All assignments relate to putting assessment skills into practice in the classroom.

title: Integrating Teaching and Learning
description: Reviews the nature and design of educational activities: theory, research, practice of unit planning, and lesson planning for active learning that meets the needs of individual students.

title: Teaching EC-6 Mathematics
description: Prepares teachers to internalize, plan, and deliver mathematics lessons appropriate for learners from early childhood through 6th grade. Candidates learn how to assess students’ mathematical knowledge and skills through a student-centered, inquiry-oriented approach. Students are introduced to methods for teaching developmentally appropriate topics in number and operations and algebra, with an emphasis on children’s mathematical thinking, conceptual understanding, and discourse. Throughout the course, candidates attend explicitly to how instruction supports students with IEPs and 504s and emergent multilingual students across different grade bands and teaching contexts.

title: Foundations of Science Education
description: Provides elementary- and middle-grades teachers with strategies to integrate science, technology, engineering, and mathematics in their classrooms.

title: Content Area Studies for Elementary School
description: Explores science, social studies, art, music, drama, and physical education content for students EC–grade six. Also, effective teaching strategies for each content area.

title: Introduction to Diverse Learners
description: A study of diversity, multicultural concepts, and inclusion. Also, explores issues, policies, and professional practice relevant to teaching.

title: Learning Environment and Professionalism: Ec-12
description: This course focuses on major issues facing teachers in establishing and maintaining a positive and productive learning environment, as well as the professional roles and responsibilities of teachers.

title: Learning to Read and Write
description: Examines principles of literacy learning in young children and predictable stages of oral language, writing, and reading development. All literacy classes require field experiences in local schools.

title: Conventional Literacy
description: Introduces theories, practices, and materials for teaching reading and/or writing in primary grades. All literacy classes require field experiences in local schools.

title: Student Teaching
description: Requires a 15-week assignment in a school that has a diverse student population and participation in a seminar on campus every 2 weeks. Students are assigned an SMU supervisor who observes in the classroom at least four times a term. A portfolio is required.

title: Student Teaching
description: Requires a 15-week assignment in a school that has a diverse student population and participation in a seminar on campus every 2 weeks. Students are assigned an SMU supervisor who observes in the classroom at least four times a term. A portfolio is required.

title: Creating Successful Classrooms
description: Students will examine current research that promotes student-centered teaching and constructivist practices. Various teaching and learning strategies of teaching in effective classrooms will be the focus of the course.

title: Content Area Methods
description: Students refine content knowledge, methods, and strategies specific to their content area and level of certification.

title: Secondary Student Teaching
description: Requires a 15-week assignment in a middle school and/or high school that has a diverse student population. Includes a seminar on campus every 2 weeks. Students are assigned an SMU supervisor who observes in the classroom at least four times a term. A portfolio is required.

title: Secondary Student Teaching
description: Requires a 15-week assignment in a middle school and/or high school that has a diverse student population. Includes a seminar on campus every 2 weeks. Students are assigned an SMU supervisor who observes in the classroom at least four times a term. A portfolio is required.

title: Internship I: High School and Middle School
description: This course requirement is a full-year assignment as the teacher of record in a public or accredited private school. Supervision by SMU faculty is required.

title: Internship II: High School and Middle School
description: This course requirement is a full-year assignment as the teacher of record in a public or accredited private school. Supervision by SMU faculty is required.

title: Methods for Teaching Algebraic Reasoning
description: Focuses on methods for teaching middle and high school mathematics, with a content focus on algebraic reasoning. Provides an opportunity to learn about secondary mathematics from a problem-solving perspective, focusing on problem-based learning and technology for teaching algebra. Various classroom routines related to algebra learning in secondary school are covered. This Covers functional relationships and their properties: patterns, variable expressions, definitions and properties of functions and graphs. Discusses various linear, quadratic, and exponential models. Includes algebraic applications of functions in everyday life, modeling, significant historical developments, rates of change, and problem-solving.

title: Methods for Teaching Geometric Reasoning
description: Focuses on methods for teaching middle and high school mathematics, with a content focus on geometric reasoning. Provides an opportunity to learn about secondary mathematics from a problem-solving perspective, focusing on problem-based learning and technology for teaching geometry. Various classroom routines related to geometry learning in secondary school are covered. Delves into Euclidean geometry; definitions; similarity; proportional reasoning; constructions; measurement; spatial reasoning; plane isometrics, translations, rotations, and reflections; dilations; significant historical developments; coordinate geometry; vectors and matrices. Introduces the two non-Euclidean geometries: elliptic and hyperbolic. Discusses practical models and available technological tools for effectively teaching students about geometry and measurement.

title: Teaching Mathematics in Elementary School 2
description: Prepares teachers to evaluate, plan, and deliver math lessons that are appropriate for learners from early childhood to 6th grade as well as how to assess student math knowledge and skills through a student-centered, inquiry approach. Students are introduced to methods for teaching all children developmentally appropriate topics in Measurement, Geometry, and Data Analysis (three of the five NCTM content Standards).

title: Internship I
description: Requires a full-year assignment as the teacher of record in a public or accredited private school. Supervision by SMU faculty is required.

title: Internship II
description: Requires a full-year assignment as the teacher of record in a public or accredited private school. Supervision by SMU faculty is required.

title: Leadership in Action
description: Expands foundational leadership understanding and philosophy and focuses on learning how to make leadership actionable through efforts that are grounded in leadership research and studies. Students learn how leadership is manifested across disciplines and beyond the campus community, as well as how to shape one’s own personal leadership journey. This course is limited to students in the Hunt Leadership Scholars Program.

title: The American University
description: Explores the development and organization of American colleges and universities. Examines higher education in conceptual forms from the perspective of students, faculty, and administrators.

title: Mathematics Methods in Special Education Course A: Pedagogical Content Across the Elementary Grades
description: This 1-credit, 15-contact-hour self-guided online course prepares students to design and deliver mathematics instruction—specifically related to fractions—for elementary students who experience or are at-risk of experiencing mathematics difficulty. Focusing on pedagogical knowledge across the elementary grades, students work through a recommended five-week pacing plan, with each week’s readings, activities, and assignments requiring approximately 3 hours. This course is equivalent to EPL 6101.
prerequisites: Restricted to students in the SCALE UP project.

title: Mathematics Methods in Special Education Course C: Upper Elementary Fraction Content
description: A 1-credit, 15-contact-hour online course that integrates and applies the pedagogical strategies and fraction content knowledge gained in EPL 5101 and EPL 5102 to optimize the development of fraction operations (e.g., addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division)for elementary students with or at-risk for mathematics difficulty. This course has a recommended five-week pacing plan, with each week’s readings, activities, and assignments requiring approximately 3 hours. This course is equivalent to EPL 6103.
prerequisites: Restricted to students in the SCALE UP project.

title: Introduction to Counseling and Human Services
description: An introduction to the counseling and human services field, emphasizing professional roles, responsibilities, and practice settings of a wide range of helping and service-oriented professions. Students explore historical and contemporary philosophies and major theoretical approaches. The course also examines professional, legal, and ethical standards applicable to diverse career paths.

title: Interpersonal Skills and Techniques
description: Designed to facilitate the development of interpersonal skills and techniques needed in personal, social, and professional interactions. Students explore and practice essential interpersonal skills, communication strategies, and techniques needed to build effective interpersonal relationships with individuals, groups, and communities.

title: Navigating Group Dynamics and Behaviors
description: Designed to provide an understanding of group dynamics and behaviors. Students explore theoretical and practical approaches for promoting positive group interactions, developing facilitation skills, and supporting group growth and development.

title: Creative Play Across the Lifespan
description: Focuses on the therapeutic benefits of play and creativity in emotional, social, and cognitive development and overall functioning from childhood through adulthood. Students explore theories and philosophies of play and evaluate play-based approaches. Emphasis is placed on experiential play and expressive activities to facilitate understanding of how creative play can be integrated to promote growth, development, and wellness.

title: Grief, Loss, and Crisis Management
description: Provides a foundation in the theories and approaches to grief, loss, and crisis intervention. Students examine philosophies and practice of crisis intervention as applied to common crisis situations.

title: Cultural Intelligence in Social Settings
description: Examines historical and current social and cultural issues. Students deepen their understanding and appreciation of human development within a multicultural and diverse framework. Focus is also given to students’ self-awareness, beliefs, values, and cultural backgrounds, and how these impact their interactions with others in social settings.
